ud6.7:1.2: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Sāvatthī, in Jeta’s Wood, at Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
ud6.7:1.3: Then at that time venerable Subhūti was sitting not far away from the Fortunate One,
ud6.7:2.1: after folding his legs crosswise, and setting his body straight, having attained a concentration free from thought. The Fortunate One saw venerable Subhūti sat not far away, after folding his legs crosswise, and setting his body straight, who had attained a concentration free from thought.
ud6.7:3.1: Then the Fortunate One, having understood the significance of it, on that occasion uttered this exalted utterance:
ud6.7:4.1: o “For he who has dispelled thoughts,
ud6.7:4.2: Totally cut (them) off within himself without remainder,
ud6.7:4.3: Perceiving the formless (nibbāna), beyond the shackle,
ud6.7:4.4: Having overcome the four yokes - he surely does not come (to birth again).”
